description: Validation at the full level (section 8). Valid datasets complete. For an invalid dataset, validate still answers status ok and reports the level failed with the refusal code (it never answers refused); a dataset that cannot be opened reports structural failed.

cases.description: fault at the profile level, validation requested at full. Rows 2 and 3 (one page) are stored in descending order.
fault at the profile level, validation requested at full. Key k04 is stored twice in one page (rows 4 and 5).
fault at the profile level, validation requested at full. Page 1 ends with k04 and page 2 starts with k03; each page is internally ascending.
fault at the profile level, validation requested at full. Row group 0 ends with k06 and row group 1 starts with k05.
fault at the profile level, validation requested at full. The last key of row group 0 equals the first key of row group 1.

fault at the profile level, validation requested at full. The first key of the only part is empty (it still sorts first). Note: The manifest cannot express an empty min key, so it names the second key; a reader that compares first keys on open may report bounds_mismatch.

fault at the structural level, validation requested at full. Row group 1 holds a 5002-byte key; pyarrow omits the whole ColumnIndex of that key chunk (statistics larger than its 4096-byte limit) but keeps the OffsetIndex.

fault at the structural level, validation requested at full. Column size is INT64 in part 0 and INT32 in part 1. Note: COL-5 requires the check no later than the first request that projects the column, so the read case projects size; structural validation checks all columns.
fault at the structural level, validation requested at full. Column h is FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY(4) in part 0 and FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY(8) in part 1.
fault at the structural level, validation requested at full. Column size is REQUIRED in part 0 and OPTIONAL in part 1.

fault at the profile level, validation requested at full. Part 0 ends with k09, part 1 starts with k05. The manifest hides this by declaring part 0's max key as k04 (so the manifest bounds look disjoint). Note: The manifest's max key for part 0 is not the actual last key, so bounds_mismatch is also a correct report.

The first data page of column size claims 3 values but holds 2. Note: No read case: a reader may decode only the values it needs from a value page, and CHECK-2's exact row count applies to key pages; full validation must find it.
